% NB: Tibskrit identifies this as —Avalokiteśvaravajrośī (?)— KCDS, p. 41. A palm-leaf Sanskrit manuscript belonging to the Potala. % The title translated into Tibetan as *Spyan ras gzigs kyi rdo rje’i smon pa* (The Vajra Aspiration of Avalokiteśvara).
The first twelve folios are:
ff. 25–26, 30–31, 36–41, and 43–44 of Daṇḍin’s *Kāvyādarśa*.
[1 recto] Siddham. Oṃ. Homage to Vajrasattva.
Delighting in the natural flavor of the churning produced by the moon-like curved cheek,
joined with the red passion of great bliss, it possesses the characteristic of innate bliss;
it is the taste of contact with the jewel of the beak, rubbed by the nectar of the vajra.
The mantra-practitioner should mutter the *hā hūṃ* mantra together with yogis who have the form of sexual union (*surata*).
% somewhat garbled as well,
% but *a*, *b*, and *c* are paralleled in the *Sādhanavidhi* manuscript.
% the "Vidyādharavinodatantra" 10\recto
This should be thoroughly compared with that text;
thus ends the instruction on retention (dhāraṇopadeśa). || 1 ||
The wind of the lower channels, resembling a harsh gale, is split;
it moves through the top of the head, like a sharp horn, reaching the summit of the command-channel.
Thus ends the instruction on killing. || 2 ||

The fragment of the cosmic egg blazes as it comes into contact with the gusts of wind from the peaks of Mount Malaya on earth, ignited by the flames of the fire that consumes the worlds of the three realms.
Thus ends the instruction on digestion (jāraṇā). || 3 ||
When the channel is being pressed, through the abandonment of death and immortality, one becomes faint;
there is a falling away of the aggregates, and the mind reels, finding bliss solely in innate joy.
Thus ends the instruction on the cause. 4.
He who makes the sky appear as if diminished by his ascetic practices,
whose full power is entirely filled with the splendor of Hara, Hari, and Hara.
Thus ends the instruction on the spreading out [of the altar]. || 5 ||

The Vidyādharas, their pride shaken by the loss of their camphor and drawn away by many [enemies], gathered together; they were repeatedly obstructed by the upward-reaching flames of the half-burnt fire from the mechanical engines.
Thus ends the *Āryāvalokiteśvaravajroli*.
